articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially rolled out GPT-5 across ChatGPT and its API, featuring significantly improved chain-of-thought reasoning, native image and audio generation, and a context window exceeding 1 million tokens. Benchmarks show substantial gains on ARC-AGI-2 and GPQA-Diamond, reigniting debate about the proximity of artificial general intelligence. The model also introduces a new "deep research agent" mode capable of multi-step tool use over extended time horizons.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Ultra Sets New Standard for Scientific Reasoning
articles.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 2.5 Ultra, which tops leaderboards in mathematical proof generation, competitive programming, and scientific literature synthesis. The model demonstrates an ability to produce novel conjectures in combinatorics that have been verified by domain experts. Google is positioning the model as a core component of its AI-for-science initiative, integrating it directly into Google Cloud research workflows.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude 4.5 Sonnet with Improved Agentic Capabilities and Computer Use
articles.summary: Anthropic released Claude 4.5 Sonnet, emphasizing reliable multi-step agentic execution, improved computer-use performance, and lower hallucination rates on factual retrieval tasks. Internal red-team evaluations show measurable gains in the model's ability to refuse unsafe instructions while maintaining helpfulness. The release includes new tooling for enterprise developers to build constrained agent pipelines with verifiable safety guarantees.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in Automotive Assembly Lines
articles.summary: Tesla announced that the third-generation Optimus humanoid robot is now operating in limited production roles at its Gigafactory in Austin, performing tasks such as bin picking, parts transport, and quality visual inspection. The robot features improved dexterous manipulation with 22-DOF hands and runs an on-board vision-language model for real-time task adaptation. Elon Musk stated the company aims to produce 10,000 units by the end of 2027 for both internal use and external sales.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Electric for Commercial Warehouse Operations
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics, backed by Hyundai, revealed the commercial version of its fully electric Atlas humanoid robot designed for logistics and warehouse environments. The platform features whole-body MPC control, dynamic obstacle avoidance, and can carry payloads up to 25 kg across unstructured terrain. Early pilot customers include DHL and Amazon, with initial deployments focused on mixed-case palletizing and facility inspection tasks.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Raises $1.5B Series C to Scale Humanoid Manufacturing
articles.summary: Figure AI closed a $1.5 billion Series C round led by Microsoft and Nvidia, valuing the humanoid robotics startup at approximately $15 billion. The funding will be used to build a dedicated robot manufacturing facility in South Carolina and to expand its foundation model for general-purpose robotic manipulation. Figure's robots are currently deployed at BMW's Spartanburg plant performing repetitive assembly tasks with demonstrated uptime exceeding 90%.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Risk Production of 1.4nm A14 Process Node Ahead of Schedule
articles.summary: TSMC announced that risk production of its A14 (1.4nm-class) process node has commenced at its Fab 20 facility in Hsinchu, approximately one quarter ahead of the original roadmap. The node uses gate-all-around nanosheet transistors and backside power delivery, promising a 15% speed improvement and 30% power reduction over N2. Major customers including Apple, Nvidia, and AMD have reportedly taped out early test chips, with volume production targeted for late 2027.

articles.title: Microsoft and Atom Computing Demonstrate Logical Qubit Error Correction Below Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Atom Computing jointly published results showing sustained below-threshold quantum error correction on a 256-logical-qubit neutral-atom system, maintaining coherent computation over 100 error correction cycles. This represents a critical engineering milestone on the path to fault-tolerant quantum computing. Microsoft announced integration of the system into its Azure Quantum platform, offering early research access to select partners working on materials science and cryptographic applications.
